Possible Outputs

From learning objective to a working digital format.

We translate content and project objectives into suitable interaction logic. The result can be delivered as a standalone web application, embedded content or part of a broader platform.

Learning Platforms

Connected learning environments with modules, resources, progress and project-specific design.

Development Process

Interaction is planned from the beginning, not added at the end.

A strong digital learning format connects project content, target group, mechanics, feedback and technical delivery.

  1. 01

    Learning Objective

    We clarify which knowledge, behaviour or reflection the output should support.

  2. 02

    Mechanics

    Suitable interactions, decisions, rules, rewards and feedback are designed.

  3. 03

    Prototype

    An early clickable or playable version makes the flow and user journey testable.

  4. 04

    Content & Testing

    Text, media, language versions and accessibility aspects are integrated and tested.

  5. 05

    Publishing

    Deployment, embedding, documentation and possible further development are organised.

Use in EU Projects

Digital outputs can support different project tasks.

The technical solution is adapted to the actual project need rather than developed as an isolated demonstration.

Workshops & Participation

Digital or hybrid tools for facilitated group work, decisions, scenarios and reflection.

What We Need to Start

Content, target group and intended impact.

A complete game design document is not required. A short description of the project topic and intended output is enough for an initial assessment.

  • Topic and learning objective
  • Target group and usage context
  • Required languages
  • Available content and media
  • Planned platform or embedding
  • Time and budget framework
Concept examples are clearly labelled

Our Digital Outputs page shows possible visual directions, mechanics and use cases. Unless an example is a completed client project, it is explicitly presented as a concept example.

Are you planning a serious game or interactive project output?

Briefly describe the topic, target group, intended output and timeline. We will assess which format may be technically and educationally appropriate.
